task.name: permuted_keyed_memory_with_registry
task.slot_permutation: Every frame independently places stable identities and readout in random slots; padding identity is -1.
task.targets: Single-link routes 0.60 times the queried value. Two-link adds 0.35 times the cyclic successor value.
task.data_separation: Fresh training, validation, test, and rollout seeds not used by v5-v7. Validation selects the action threshold. The sealed test split is evaluated once after strategy and threshold selection.

model.candidate_set: All present memory identities sorted by persistent registry ID to the current readout identity; candidate shape is fixed by memory_count.
model.neuron_parameter_sharing: One ModelNeuron module and one neuron weight set are reused at every stable neuron identity; recurrent state remains identity-specific.
model.aggregation: Incoming messages are aggregated inside the shared ModelNeuron; aggregation is not an independently parameterized model.
model.external_parameters: Link proposal policy and scalar task readout are separate graph-level/task-level components and are not per-neuron weights.

training.topology_gradient: Task-loss-only soft candidate route training; hard actions are evaluated after training. No edge/action labels or sparsity penalty.
training.implementation_note: MPS hot path uses stable-ID fixed-shape candidates, skips redundant value validation for generated in-contract inputs, and remaps minibatch edge indices with tensor operations.
training.batch_implementation: per_sample_gradient_accumulation; one graph per ModelNeuronGraph forward

validation_selection.rule: Maximize weighted mean of edge F1 and macro recall for operation classes present in validation; tie-break by lower validation MSE, then higher confidence threshold.

evolution.topology_policy: Each rollout fixes a neuron identity cohort for all frames, varies queries and slot permutations, carries hard topology between frames, and remaps by persisted identity.

decision_rules.quality_ci: Paired per-seed relative MSE delta; 95% two-sided t interval upper bound must be below zero.
decision_rules.interpretation: Fixed before the new test set is evaluated. Validation may select only the action confidence threshold.

controls.parameter_matched: Stable-identity-canonicalized flat MLP with nearest integer hidden width to graph parameter count.
controls.linear_mac_matched: Stable-identity-canonicalized flat MLP with nearest integer hidden width to graph Linear MAC count.
controls.linear_mac_contract: Counts Linear output elements times input width, batch size one. Multiply-add FLOPs subtotal is 2x this count; scatter, reductions, pointwise operations, activations, optimizer, memory traffic and backend fusion are excluded.
controls.identity_canonicalization: Decode task key bits and scatter valid neurons into canonical identity slots; registry IDs remain separate from input feature identity.

cost_accounting.flops_scope: Report exact Linear MAC subtotal and 2x multiply-add subtotal. Do not claim total FLOPs: installed PyTorch MPS build exposes CPU profiler activity only, while sparse index_add/scatter, nonlinear and optimizer operations are not covered by the Linear subtotal.

diagnostics.gradient_coverage: Capture connected, finite, nonzero parameter gradients on the first microbatch before the optimizer update.

limitations: Synthetic key-value retrieval/composition does not establish language or broad capability claims.
The neuron model has one shared parameter set across all graph positions; independent state is not a per-neuron weight set.
Pool sizes cover 4 to 64 memory neurons and do not establish asymptotic scaling.
Identity persistence is a local atomic JSON contract; concurrent writers and remote stores are outside this test.
Host and MPS memory are sampled and may miss transient peaks.
Total MPS FLOPs are not exactly countable in this PyTorch build; Linear MAC and multiply-add subtotals are reported separately.
A batch is represented as gradient accumulation across independent one-graph forwards; it is not graph-batched/vectorized.
The evaluation oracle is an upper-bound control derived from labels and is not an inference adapter or deployable model.
